title: Concatenating and Splitting Tensors
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of concatenating and splitting tensors in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of concatenating and splitting tensors and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Concatenating and Splitting Tensors: Tensor shape is not the same as physical memory layout. Strides describe how indexing steps through storage, while views may share storage with an existing tensor. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding layout helps explain when an operation returns a view, when a copy is necessary, and why some reshapes or in-place edits behave unexpectedly. For this lesson, focus on torch.cat() and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Compare shape and storage: transpose-like operations may produce non-contiguous views, while contiguous() can materialize a contiguous copy when required. The source topics for this lesson are: torch.cat(), torch.stack(), torch.split() and torch.chunk(). Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
import torch
a = torch.tensor([1, 2])
b = torch.tensor([3, 4])
print(torch.cat((a, b)).tolist())
print(torch.stack((a, b)).shape)

troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not assume every view owns independent memory or that contiguous() is free; both aliasing and copies matter.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
